correctness.rationale: For every point the positive and negative root branches have exactly 4/h and (N-4)/h distinct hypotheses. A depth-three tree requires h=1 and a 2/2 split of its four positive hypotheses, equivalent to some nonzero two-point translate intersection. With such an overlap, the four joint trace cells have sizes 2,2,2,N-6; N>=8 ensures all can each make one further distinguishing split. A depth-four tree is impossible. The h=2 and h=4 cases are proved separately. For prime order>=11 a lag with 3 intersection points yields a length-three path and a lag 2t with exactly 2, yielding the Sidon dichotomy. The 52-count uses exhaustive 55 normalized candidate pairs and a 13-to-1 translation normalization. The standalone exact recursive checker verified all four-seeds for 14 finite groups, including noncyclic groups and all prime-thirteen seeds.

value.rationale: This natural complete structural classification holds across all finite abelian groups of order at least eight and distinguishes multiplicity-two crossings from higher overlaps and stabilizer symmetries. It connects adaptive online shattering to additive Sidon geometry and identifies the first prime where a Sidon four-seed suppresses depth three. A concrete same-VC/different-Littlestone pair demonstrates additional information unavailable from static VC dimension; the composite-order boundary rules out an overgeneralized Sidon substitution.
